e-5486.knowledge_point: Calculating the Eigenvalues of a 3x3 Matrix Containing a Block of Zeros
e-5486.problem:
Determine all real eigenvalues $\lambda$ of the matrix 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069304/assets/9c2a25dabbe750ebb52b4de6dbee954df55c09a8ceaf0b82eef346b5a337c544.png)
e-5486.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\, A-\lambda I \mathbin{:}$
﻿﻿﻿![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069304/assets/947389b453c22e1b56704ec6a1cdf8e7e529ea9a944c57d3e55a471ab3539569.png)

The characteristic equation is $\det(A-\lambda I) = 0.$ 

Since the determinant of a triangular (or diagonal) matrix is given by the product of the entries on the main diagonal, we obtain the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-9-\lambda  & 4 & 8 \\ 0 & 9-\lambda  & -7 \\ 0 & 0 & 6-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-9-\lambda )(9-\lambda )(6-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (\lambda +9)(\lambda -9)(\lambda -6) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are $\lambda_1=-9,$ $\lambda_2=9,$ and $\lambda_3=6.$ 

**Note:** The eigenvalues of a triangular (or diagonal) matrix are always the entries on the main diagonal.

e-7047.knowledge_point: Calculating the Eigenvalues of a 4x4 Matrix Containing a Block of Zeros
e-7047.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069304/assets/2379f9f0cec3f257da5a4c0695f114d0bc7f3b4c914edabfd690ff94705faceb.png)

Consider the matrix $P$ given above. Which of the following statements are true?

- $\lambda=4$ is an eigenvalue of $P$

- $\lambda=-1$ is an eigenvalue of $P$

- The eigenvalue $\lambda=6$ has algebraic multiplicity $2$
e-7047.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\, P-\lambda I \mathbin{:}$
﻿﻿﻿![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069304/assets/8ee9ef991440e5641d6a458c0384382b54eb3d8504856b942fc33cf24b0b85e9.png)

The characteristic equation is $\det(P-\lambda I) = 0.$ 

Notice that we can expand the $4 \times 4$ determinant across the $1$st column, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(P-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & 0 & -8 & -2 \\ 0 & -1-\lambda  & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 4-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 7 & -3 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 4-\lambda  & 0 \\ 7 & -3 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, expanding the $3 \times 3$ determinant across the $2$nd row, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}(3-\lambda )\cdot (4-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 5 \\ 7 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )(4-\lambda )((-1-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-35) & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )(4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-36) & =0 \\ (\lambda -3)(\lambda -4)(\lambda -6)(\lambda +6) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the eigenvalues of $P$ are $\lambda=3,$ $\lambda=4,$ $\lambda=6,$ and $\lambda=-6$ (all with algebraic multiplicity $1$).

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$B=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -3 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,B-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
B-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & -2-\lambda  & 0 \\ -3 & 5 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(B-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $2$nd row, we obtain the following:  

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & -4 & 3 \\ 0 & -2-\lambda  & 0 \\ -3 & 5 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-2-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 3 \\ -3 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-2-\lambda )((1-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-(3)(-3)) & =0 \\ (\lambda +2)({\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda +10) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Determine all real eigenvalues $\lambda $ of the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 3 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 6\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,A-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 3-\lambda  & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 6-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(A-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Since the determinant of a triangular (or diagonal) matrix is given by the product of the entries on the main diagonal, we obtain the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ -5 & 3-\lambda  & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 6-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )(3-\lambda )(6-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (\lambda -4)(\lambda -3)(\lambda -6) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=3,$ $\,{\lambda }_{2}=4,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=6.$

**Note:** The eigenvalues of a triangular (or diagonal) matrix are always the entries on the main diagonal.

before.html:
Question 3
?

Find the characteristic equation of the matrix B=[8100−5−706−93].

a
(λ−8)(λ+7)(λ−3)=0
b
λ(λ−6)(λ+7)=0
c
(λ−3)(λ−3)(λ+2)=0
d
(λ−3)(λ−6)(λ+1)=0
e
(λ+3)(λ−3)(λ+2)=0
Submit

decision.explanation: Expanding det(B−λI) along the third column gives (3−λ)((8−λ)(−7−λ)+50)=(3−λ)(λ²−λ−6). Since λ²−λ−6=(λ−3)(λ+2), the characteristic equation is (λ−3)²(λ+2)=0, matching option c.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$B=[\begin{aligned}8 & 10 & 0 \\ -5 & -7 & 0 \\ 6 & -9 & 3\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,B-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
B-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 10 & 0 \\ -5 & -7-\lambda  & 0 \\ 6 & -9 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(B-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $3$rd column, we obtain the following:  

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 10 & 0 \\ -5 & -7-\lambda  & 0 \\ 6 & -9 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 10 \\ -5 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )((8-\lambda )(-7-\lambda )-(-5)(10)) & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -6) & =0 \\ (\lambda -3)(\lambda -3)(\lambda +2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

a
(λ−8)(λ+7)(λ−3)=0
b
λ(λ−6)(λ+7)=0
c
(λ−3)(λ−3)(λ+2)=0
d
(λ−3)(λ−6)(λ+1)=0
e
(λ+3)(λ−3)(λ+2)=0

Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we find the matrix B−λI: ﻿﻿﻿B−λI=[8−λ100−5−7−λ06−93−λ]

The characteristic equation is det(B−λI)=0.

Expanding the determinant across the 3rd column, we obtain the following:

det(B−λI)=0|8−λ100−5−7−λ06−93−λ|=0(3−λ)|8−λ10−5−7−λ|=0(3−λ)((8−λ)(−7−λ)−(−5)(10))=0(3−λ)(λ2−λ−6)=0(λ−3)(λ−3)(λ+2)=0

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Eigenvalues of a 3x3 Matrix Containing a Block of Zeros
content.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$B=[\begin{aligned}8 & 10 & 0 \\ -5 & -7 & 0 \\ 6 & -9 & 3\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,B-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
B-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 10 & 0 \\ -5 & -7-\lambda  & 0 \\ 6 & -9 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(B-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $3$rd column, we obtain the following:  

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 10 & 0 \\ -5 & -7-\lambda  & 0 \\ 6 & -9 & 3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 10 \\ -5 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )((8-\lambda )(-7-\lambda )-(-5)(10)) & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -6) & =0 \\ (\lambda -3)(\lambda -3)(\lambda +2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4

Find the characteristic equation of the matrix A=[−20−21−1−1−201].

a
(λ+1)(λ+3)(λ−2)=0
b
(λ−1)(λ−3)(λ−2)=0
c
(λ+1)(λ−1)(λ+1)=0
d
(λ−1)(λ+3)(λ−2)=0
e
λ(λ−2)(λ+2)=0
Submit

decision.explanation: Expanding det(A−λI) along the second column gives (−1−λ)((−2−λ)(1−λ)−4)=−(λ+1)(λ²+λ−6)=−(λ+1)(λ+3)(λ−2). Setting this equal to zero gives option a.

after.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,A-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & -1-\lambda  & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(A-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $2$nd column, we obtain the following:  

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & -1-\lambda  & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & -2 \\ -2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )((-2-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-(-2)(-2)) & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+\lambda -6) & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)(\lambda +3)(\lambda -2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

$A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,A-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & -1-\lambda  & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(A-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $2$nd column, we obtain the following:  

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & -1-\lambda  & -1 \\ -2 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & -2 \\ -2 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )((-2-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-(-2)(-2)) & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+\lambda -6) & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)(\lambda +3)(\lambda -2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Find the characteristic equation of the matrix A=[−32−1523001].

a
(1−λ)(λ2+λ−16)=0
b
(1−λ)(λ2−16)=0
c
(1−λ)(λ2+λ+4)=0
d
(1−λ)(λ2+λ−10)=0
e
(1−λ)(λ2+λ−4)=0
Submit

decision.explanation: Expanding det(A−λI) along the third row gives (1−λ)((−3−λ)(2−λ)−10)=(1−λ)(λ²+λ−16). Setting this equal to zero gives option a.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & -1 \\ 5 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,A-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-3-\lambda  & 2 & -1 \\ 5 & 2-\lambda  & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(A-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $3$rd row, we obtain the following:  

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-3-\lambda  & 2 & -1 \\ 5 & 2-\lambda  & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-3-\lambda  & 2 \\ 5 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )((-3-\lambda )(2-\lambda )-2\cdot 5) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+\lambda -16) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Eigenvalues of a 3x3 Matrix Containing a Block of Zeros
content.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & -1 \\ 5 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,A-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-3-\lambda  & 2 & -1 \\ 5 & 2-\lambda  & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(A-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $3$rd row, we obtain the following:  

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-3-\lambda  & 2 & -1 \\ 5 & 2-\lambda  & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-3-\lambda  & 2 \\ 5 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )((-3-\lambda )(2-\lambda )-2\cdot 5) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+\lambda -16) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -6 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & -3 & -4 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $P$ given above. Which of the following statements are true?

- $\lambda =0$ is an eigenvalue of $P$
- $\lambda =-4$ is an eigenvalue of $P$
- The eigenvalue $\lambda =2$ has algebraic multiplicity $2$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,P-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
P-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & 2 & -6 & 8 \\ 0 & -\lambda  & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & -3 & -4-\lambda  & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(P-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Notice that we can expand the $4\times 4$ determinant across the $1$st column, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(P-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & 2 & -6 & 8 \\ 0 & -\lambda  & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & -3 & -4-\lambda  & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-\lambda  & 0 & 7 \\ -3 & -4-\lambda  & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, expanding the $3\times 3$ determinant across the $3$rd row, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}(5-\lambda )\cdot (2-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-\lambda  & 0 \\ -3 & -4-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )(2-\lambda )(-\lambda )(-4-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (\lambda -5)(\lambda -2)\lambda (\lambda +4) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the eigenvalues of $P$ are $\lambda =5,$ $\lambda =2,$ $\lambda =0,$ and $\lambda =-4$  (all with algebraic multiplicity $1$).

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."

Find the characteristic equation of the matrix A=[60000−7000060000−2].

a
(λ−6)(λ+6)(λ+7)(λ+2)=0
b
(λ−6)(λ+6)(λ−7)(λ−2)=0
c
(λ−6)(λ+7)(λ+2)=0
d
(λ−6)2(λ−7)(λ−2)=0
e
(λ−6)2(λ+7)(λ+2)=0
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we find the matrix A−λI: ﻿﻿﻿A−λI=[6−λ0000−7−λ00006−λ0000−2−λ]

The characteristic equation is det(A−λI)=0.

Since the determinant of a triangular (or diagonal) matrix is given by the product of the entries on the main diagonal, we obtain the following: det(A−λI)=0|6−λ0000−7−λ00006−λ0000−2−λ|=0(6−λ)(−7−λ)(6−λ)(−2−λ)=0(λ−6)2(λ+7)(λ+2)=0

verification.explanation: The diagonal determinant is (6−λ)²(−7−λ)(−2−λ)=(λ−6)²(λ+7)(λ+2). The revealed solution confirms option e, including the repeated factor for eigenvalue 6.

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Eigenvalues of a 4x4 Matrix Containing a Block of Zeros
content.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,A-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}6-\lambda  & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -7-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 6-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(A-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Since the determinant of a triangular (or diagonal) matrix is given by the product of the entries on the main diagonal, we obtain the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}6-\lambda  & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -7-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 6-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (6-\lambda )(-7-\lambda )(6-\lambda )(-2-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (\lambda -6)^{2}(\lambda +7)(\lambda +2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Find the characteristic equation of the matrix P=[76−100−40800311000−5].

a
(λ−7)(λ+4)(λ+5)=0
b
(λ+7)(λ+4)(λ−3)(λ−2)=0
c
(λ−7)(λ+4)(λ−3)(λ−5)=0
d
(λ−7)(λ+4)(λ−3)(λ+5)=0
e
(λ−1)(λ+4)(λ−8)(λ+5)=0
Submit

decision.explanation: P is upper triangular, so det(P−λI)=(7−λ)(−4−λ)(3−λ)(−5−λ)=(λ−7)(λ+4)(λ−3)(λ+5). Setting this equal to zero gives option d.

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$P=[\begin{aligned}7 & 6 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,P-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
P-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}7-\lambda  & 6 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4-\lambda  & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 3-\lambda  & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -5-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(P-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Since the determinant of a triangular (or diagonal) matrix is given by the product of the entries on the main diagonal, we obtain the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}det(P-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}7-\lambda  & 6 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4-\lambda  & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 3-\lambda  & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (7-\lambda )(-4-\lambda )(3-\lambda )(-5-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (\lambda -7)(\lambda +4)(\lambda -3)(\lambda +5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Calculating the Eigenvalues of a 4x4 Matrix Containing a Block of Zeros
content.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$P=[\begin{aligned}7 & 6 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -5\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,P-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
P-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}7-\lambda  & 6 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4-\lambda  & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 3-\lambda  & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -5-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(P-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Since the determinant of a triangular (or diagonal) matrix is given by the product of the entries on the main diagonal, we obtain the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}det(P-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}7-\lambda  & 6 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4-\lambda  & 0 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 3-\lambda  & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (7-\lambda )(-4-\lambda )(3-\lambda )(-5-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (\lambda -7)(\lambda +4)(\lambda -3)(\lambda +5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 11
?

Find the characteristic equation of the matrix C=[3−1−11−3312−2].

a
λ3−2λ2−13λ+25=0
b
λ3+2λ2+13λ−15=0
c
λ3+2λ2−13λ+10=0
d
λ3+13λ2+2λ+4=0
e
λ3−2λ2−13λ−30=0
Submit

decision.explanation: Expanding det(C−λI) along the first row gives (3−λ)(λ²+5λ)+(−5−λ)−(5+λ)=−λ³−2λ²+13λ−10. Setting this equal to zero and multiplying by −1 yields option c.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$C=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -3 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,C-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
C-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -3-\lambda  & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(C-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $1$st row, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(C-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -3-\lambda  & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-3-\lambda  & 3 \\ 2 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}|-(-1)|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}|+(-1)|\begin{aligned}1 & -3-\lambda  \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+5\lambda )+(-\lambda -5)-(5+\lambda ) & =0 \\ (-{\lambda }^{3}-2{\lambda }^{2}+15\lambda )-\lambda -5-5-\lambda  & =0 \\ -{\lambda }^{3}-2{\lambda }^{2}+13\lambda -10 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{3}+2{\lambda }^{2}-13\lambda +10 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Eigenvalues of a General 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$C=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -3 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,C-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
C-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -3-\lambda  & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(C-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $1$st row, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(C-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -3-\lambda  & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-3-\lambda  & 3 \\ 2 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}|-(-1)|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}|+(-1)|\begin{aligned}1 & -3-\lambda  \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (3-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+5\lambda )+(-\lambda -5)-(5+\lambda ) & =0 \\ (-{\lambda }^{3}-2{\lambda }^{2}+15\lambda )-\lambda -5-5-\lambda  & =0 \\ -{\lambda }^{3}-2{\lambda }^{2}+13\lambda -10 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{3}+2{\lambda }^{2}-13\lambda +10 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 12
after.problem:
Determine all real eigenvalues $\lambda $ of the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,A-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2-\lambda  & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is given by $det(A-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $1$st row, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2-\lambda  & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 1 \\ 3 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-{\lambda }^{3}+6\lambda +5)-(-1-\lambda ) & =0 \\ -{\lambda }^{3}+7\lambda +6 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{3}-7\lambda -6 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to solve this equation. We find the first root by testing some values. According to the rational zeros theorem, a list of good first guesses consists of all divisors of $6:$ 

$$
\pm 1,\pm 2,\pm 3,\pm 6
$$

- Let's pick $x=1.$ Substituting to the characteristic equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(1)^{3}-7(1)-6 & =-12.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $\lambda =1$ is not a root of the equation.

- Let's pick $x=-1.$ Substituting to the characteristic equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(-1)^{3}-7(-1)-6 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $\lambda =-1$ is a root of the equation.

So, we can factor $(\lambda +1)$ out of ${\lambda }^{3}-7\lambda -6$ using synthetic division:

| $-1$ | $1$ | $0$ | $-7$ | $-6$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | $↓$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $6$ |
|  | $1$ | $-1$ | $-6$ | $0$ |

So, we obtain the following factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\lambda +1)({\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -6) & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)(\lambda +2)(\lambda -3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=-1,$ $\,{\lambda }_{2}=-2,\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}=3.$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Eigenvalues of a General 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
Determine all real eigenvalues $\lambda $ of the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,A-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
A-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2-\lambda  & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is given by $det(A-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $1$st row, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2-\lambda  & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & 1 \\ 3 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-{\lambda }^{3}+6\lambda +5)-(-1-\lambda ) & =0 \\ -{\lambda }^{3}+7\lambda +6 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{3}-7\lambda -6 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to solve this equation. We find the first root by testing some values. According to the rational zeros theorem, a list of good first guesses consists of all divisors of $6:$ 

$$
\pm 1,\pm 2,\pm 3,\pm 6
$$

- Let's pick $x=1.$ Substituting to the characteristic equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(1)^{3}-7(1)-6 & =-12.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $\lambda =1$ is not a root of the equation.

- Let's pick $x=-1.$ Substituting to the characteristic equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(-1)^{3}-7(-1)-6 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $\lambda =-1$ is a root of the equation.

So, we can factor $(\lambda +1)$ out of ${\lambda }^{3}-7\lambda -6$ using synthetic division:

| $-1$ | $1$ | $0$ | $-7$ | $-6$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | $↓$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $6$ |
|  | $1$ | $-1$ | $-6$ | $0$ |

So, we obtain the following factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\lambda +1)({\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -6) & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)(\lambda +2)(\lambda -3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=-1,$ $\,{\lambda }_{2}=-2,\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}=3.$

Find the characteristic equation of the matrix B=[−99005−8−210].

a
λ3+4λ2−37λ−72=0
b
λ3+4λ2−37λ−108=0
c
λ3+4λ2−53λ−36=0
d
λ3−4λ2+53λ+36=0
e
λ3−4λ2−37λ+72=0
Submit

decision.explanation: Expanding det(B−λI) along the first row gives (−9−λ)(λ²−5λ+8)+144=−λ³−4λ²+37λ+72. Setting this equal to zero and multiplying by −1 gives λ³+4λ²−37λ−72=0, matching option a.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$B=[\begin{aligned}-9 & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -8 \\ -2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,B-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
B-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-9-\lambda  & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 5-\lambda  & -8 \\ -2 & 1 & -\lambda \end{aligned}].
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(B-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $1$st row, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-9-\lambda  & 9 & 0 \\ 0 & 5-\lambda  & -8 \\ -2 & 1 & -\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-9-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & -8 \\ 1 & -\lambda \end{aligned}|-9|\begin{aligned}0 & -8 \\ -2 & -\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-9-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-5\lambda +8)-9(-16) & =0 \\ (-{\lambda }^{3}-4{\lambda }^{2}+37\lambda -72)+144 & =0 \\ -{\lambda }^{3}-4{\lambda }^{2}+37\lambda +72 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{3}+4{\lambda }^{2}-37\lambda -72 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 14
after.problem:
Determine all real eigenvalues $\lambda $ of the matrix 
$O=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,O-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
O-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1-\lambda  & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is given by $det(O-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $1$st row, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(O-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1-\lambda  & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 1 \\ 1 & -\lambda \end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}0 & -1-\lambda  \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-{\lambda }^{3}-2{\lambda }^{2}+1)+(\lambda +1) & =0 \\ -{\lambda }^{3}-2{\lambda }^{2}+\lambda +2 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{3}+2{\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to solve this equation. We find the first root by testing some values. According to the rational zeros theorem, a list of good first guesses consists of all divisors of $2:$ 

$$
\pm 1,\pm 2
$$

Let's pick $x=1.$ Substituting to the characteristic equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(1)^{3}+2(1)^{2}-(1)-2 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $\lambda =1$ is a root of the equation. So, we can factor $(\lambda -1)$ out of ${\lambda }^{3}+2{\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -2$ using synthetic division:

| $1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $-1$ | $-2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | $↓$ | $1$ | $3$ | $2$ |
|  | $1$ | $3$ | $2$ | $0$ |

So, we obtain the following factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\lambda -1)({\lambda }^{2}+3\lambda +2) & =0 \\ (\lambda -1)(\lambda +2)(\lambda +1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=1,$ $\,{\lambda }_{2}=-2,\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}=-1.$

\begin{aligned}det(O-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -1-\lambda  & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 1 \\ 1 & -\lambda \end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}0 & -1-\lambda  \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-{\lambda }^{3}-2{\lambda }^{2}+1)+(\lambda +1) & =0 \\ -{\lambda }^{3}-2{\lambda }^{2}+\lambda +2 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{3}+2{\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to solve this equation. We find the first root by testing some values. According to the rational zeros theorem, a list of good first guesses consists of all divisors of $2:$ 

$$
\pm 1,\pm 2
$$

Let's pick $x=1.$ Substituting to the characteristic equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(1)^{3}+2(1)^{2}-(1)-2 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $\lambda =1$ is a root of the equation. So, we can factor $(\lambda -1)$ out of ${\lambda }^{3}+2{\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -2$ using synthetic division:

| $1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $-1$ | $-2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | $↓$ | $1$ | $3$ | $2$ |
|  | $1$ | $3$ | $2$ | $0$ |

So, we obtain the following factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}(\lambda -1)({\lambda }^{2}+3\lambda +2) & =0 \\ (\lambda -1)(\lambda +2)(\lambda +1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=1,$ $\,{\lambda }_{2}=-2,\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}=-1.$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Eigenvalues of a General 3x3 Matrix
content.problem:
Find the characteristic equation of the matrix 
$B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -8 & -4 \\ 3 & 8 & 3 \\ -6 & -10 & -3\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,B-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
B-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & -8 & -4 \\ 3 & 8-\lambda  & 3 \\ -6 & -10 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(B-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Expanding the determinant across the $1$st row, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & -8 & -4 \\ 3 & 8-\lambda  & 3 \\ -6 & -10 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 3 \\ -10 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}|-(-8)|\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ -6 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}|+(-4)|\begin{aligned}3 & 8-\lambda  \\ -6 & -10\end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-5\lambda +6)+8(-3\lambda +9)-4(-6\lambda +18) & =0 \\ (-{\lambda }^{3}+4{\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -6)+(-24\lambda +72)-(-24\lambda +72) & =0 \\ -{\lambda }^{3}+4{\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -6 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{3}-4{\lambda }^{2}+\lambda +6 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
